transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because my head just… it doesn’t stay on task anymore. Like at work, I’ll be doing inventory and lose track, or I’ll go to the supply closet and forget what I went in there for. And when I try studying for this supervisor certification, I end up reading the same line over and over. It’s getting frustrating.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… most days, I do. It’s like there’s this heavy, flat feeling that just kind of follows me around. Even when I’m just pushing my cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family trying to act normal, it’s still there.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I still do the things I usually do, but I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m enjoying them less. It’s hard to say.
Did you have trouble paying attention like this when you were a child?

Not that I really remember. This feels more like something that’s been happening now. I’ll be doing inventory or trying to study for that supervisor certification, and my mind just won’t stay on it—like I keep reading the same line or I forget why I went into the supply closet.
How long have you been feeling down like this?
About three years now, I think. It started around when the contractor switched us to rotating evening and overnight shifts at the bigger properties. Since then it’s just kind of stayed with me.
Do you feel this low mood is mainly because of the rotating evening and overnight shifts?
Yeah, I think that’s when it started. Since they switched us to rotating evenings and overnights at the larger properties, it’s been going on about three years now.
Since your work shifts changed, have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah. My sleep’s been pretty messed up for a long time. After an overnight shift I’ll get home exhausted, but then I’m just lying there, tired but wired. And even when I do sleep for a decent amount of time, I wake up feeling like I barely rested.
If you were working a regular daytime schedule, do you think your sleep would still be a problem?

I’m not really sure. The overnights definitely make it worse, but my sleep has been messed up for so long now that I don’t know if a daytime schedule would fix it. Even when I get enough hours, I still wake up feeling like I didn’t really rest.
Do you often feel hopeless?

Yeah… a lot of days I do. It’s not always like I’m thinking something dramatic, it’s more this heavy, flat feeling that kind of follows me around. Even when I’m at work just pushing the cart down an empty hallway, or at home with my family trying to act normal, it’s still there.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living?
I don’t know… I guess I’ve had moments where I wonder what the point is, but I’m not sure I’d say I think life isn’t worth living. It’s more like I feel worn down and stuck.
For at least two weeks at a time, have you felt depressed most of the day nearly every day?

Yeah. I’d say that happens pretty often for me. Most days, for a long stretch at a time, I have this heavy, kind of flat feeling that just follows me around. Even if I’m just pushing the cart down an empty hallway at work, or sitting with my family trying to act normal, it’s still there.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying about different things?
I’m not sure I’d say a lot. I worry about things sometimes, like anyone, but I haven’t really noticed it being the main thing for me.
Lately, have you been getting less enjoyment from things you usually like to do?
I’m not really sure. I guess I haven’t paid attention to it that way. Some things feel harder to get into, but I don’t know if I’d say I’m getting less enjoyment across the board.
Have you noticed your appetite changing?
I haven’t really noticed a big change, no. I mean, some days I eat more or less just depending on the day, but nothing that stands out to me.
Have you ever gone for several days needing much less sleep than usual and still felt full of energy?
Not really, no. I can’t think of a time where I needed way less sleep for several days and still felt full of energy.
During one of those low periods, have you ever had trouble sleeping nearly every night for at least two weeks?

Yeah, I’d say so. My sleep’s been messed up for a long time. After an overnight shift I’ll be exhausted, but then I lie there kind of tired and wired. And even when I do get a decent amount of hours, I wake up feeling like I barely rested.
When you have time away from work for a few days, does that heavy, flat feeling go away?

No, not really. Even if I’m off work for a few days, it’s still there. It’s like this heavy, flat feeling follows me around, whether I’m at work pushing the cart down the hallway or just sitting at home with my family trying to seem normal.
When you’re in those low periods, do you feel slowed down in your body or movements?
I’m not really sure. I don’t think I’ve noticed my movements being especially slowed down. I mean, I feel heavy and low, but I can still get around and do what I need to do.
Have you been feeling tired or low on energy most days?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I mean, I do feel worn out a lot, but I haven’t really been keeping track of whether it’s most days or not.
Would you say you feel tired or low on energy most days?

I guess I don’t really know. I feel tired a lot, yeah, but I haven’t been paying attention enough to say if it’s most days. It kind of comes with everything feeling heavy, but I’m not sure how often exactly.
